guarantees.claim: For the interface index i equal to app_id, app_o[i].ready = app_data_ready | fsm_data_ready, app_o[i].done = app_digest_done | fsm_digest_done_q, app_o[i].digest_share0 = app_digest[0], app_o[i].digest_share1 = app_digest[1], app_o[i].error = error_i | fsm_digest_done_q | sparse_fsm_error_o | service_rejected_error.
guarantees.cond: i == app_id (combinational, always active when condition true)

guarantees.claim: For all interface indices i not equal to app_id, app_o[i] fields are driven to 0 (ready, done, error = 0, digest_share0 = 0, digest_share1 = 0).

assumptions.claim: app_id must be a valid index: 0 ≤ app_id < NumAppIntf.
assumptions.risk: If app_id is out of range, no interface is selected and all app_o outputs remain zero, masking all ready/done/digest/error information from the application.

uncertain_points.claim: Is app_id a compile-time constant (parameter) or a run-time input? The chunk uses it as a signal in an always_comb loop, but the context hints at a generate if (i == app_id). This determines whether the interface selection is static or dynamic.
uncertain_points.risk: If app_id is a dynamic input, combinational selection may cause glitches or transient wrong interface activation, potentially exposing digest shares or error to the wrong interface.

uncertain_points.claim: fsm_digest_done_q is ORed into both done and error outputs. The comment says 'if fsm asserts done, should be an error case', but the same signal also acts as a valid done indicator. This dual use may confuse receivers about completion versus error.
uncertain_points.risk: A receiver may interpret the simultaneous done=1 and error=1 as an error condition and discard a valid digest, causing data loss.
